visual_thesis: Token price is only one part of completed-work cost. Compare the same task and acceptable output while exposing retries, human review and recovery; vendor benchmark claims require local validation.
mechanism_metaphor: A single exploded task specimen is opened like a scientific sample with four unequal nested material strata. At entry one representative task sheet explicitly says Same task, beside an acceptance stencil labeled Acceptable output. A model-processing segment feeds a result specimen; under it lie a folded retry segment, a review-time band, and a recovery segment. The resulting completed-work specimen is larger because it contains those cost categories, not because of an invented measured ratio. The object remains continuous via two thin headless alignment pins. A small detached publisher-claim sample at upper right is clearly labeled Vendor benchmarks and has no graph, price, badge or score. Twelve meaningful parts: fixed task leaf, acceptance stencil, input aperture, model layer, output specimen, retry fold, review band, recovery layer, completed-task assembly, two alignment pins, and detached claim sample. Each cost-bearing stratum has its specific label; no opaque blank cost ledger, fake currency or numeric measurements. One causal arrow from same-task specimen port to the task-test aperture; no other arrowheads.

editorial_style_plan.difference_from_earlier_story_images: Unlike November 19 Neon’s two ribbon races into a score board, this matte scientific specimen exposes unmeasured retry, review and recovery strata inside a single completed task; it has no quantitative race or ledger.
